content: Weston General Hospital is a district general hospital located in Weston-super-Mare, North Somerset, England. It operates under the Weston Area Health NHS Trust (WAHT). The hospital provides a range of services, including an Accident & Emergency department, an intensive care unit, an Oncology and Haematology day unit, and a day case unit. It has a total of 358 beds and employs approximately 1,800 staff members. Notably, it houses the largest midwifery-led maternity unit in the country. Additionally, the hospital operates a private 12-bed unit called The Waterside Suite, which is fully owned by the hospital trust. Profits generated from this private unit are reinvested into the main hospital. The Healthcare Commission, an independent body responsible for promoting quality healthcare in the UK, has evaluated Weston General Hospital's performance. During the 2005/2006 period, the hospital's quality of healthcare was rated as weak on a four-point scale (weak, fair, good, excellent), placing it among the bottom 9% of NHS trusts in the country. Its use of resources was also rated as weak, ranking it in the bottom 37% of trusts. In the 2006/2007 period, the hospital's quality of healthcare rating improved to fair, but its use of resources remained weak. The hospital has faced challenges with hospital-acquired infections, including Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and Clostridium difficile (C. diff). In 2003, the trust recorded the highest rate of MRSA infections in the country. In August 2007, the hospital faced criticism following the death of a 75-year-old cancer patient due to C. diff. In response, the hospital reported a 25% reduction in infection rates throughout 2007. By September 2007, the trust released data showing further improvements, with only one case of MRSA and 18 cases of C. diff in August, compared to over 30 cases earlier in the year. These improvements were attributed to the implementation of a bare below the elbow policy, which emphasized proper hand and wrist hygiene among staff, as well as regular steam cleaning of patient beds. An independent inquiry in 2004 confirmed that such manipulation had occurred. In 2006, one of the managers implicated in the allegations lost a libel case against the BBC, which had accused her of involvement in falsifying waiting lists. Despite these issues, waiting times for treatment remain a challenge. In 2006, Weston General Hospital was one of only eight hospitals in the country that failed to meet targets for reducing waiting times. The hospital has a rich history. The Queen Alexandra Memorial Hospital, located on The Boulevard, was officially opened in 1928 by the Duke and Duchess of York (later King George VI and Queen Elizabeth, the Queen Mother). Over time, the hospital expanded with the addition of new equipment and temporary buildings to meet the growing needs of the community. However, as the town of Weston-super-Mare grew, particularly in the Worle area, it became clear that a new hospital was needed. After much debate, a new hospital was constructed and officially opened on September 16, 1986, on the outskirts of Uphill village. In January 2003, the hospital opened the Jackson Barstow Wing, a new Oncology and Haematology day unit designed to serve patients from the surrounding area. This unit allowed patients to receive treatments such as chemotherapy and blood transfusions locally, without needing to travel to Bristol. In February 2007, Weston General Hospital opened the Seashore Centre, a new paediatric unit featuring outpatient services and a 10-bed day ward. This unit was established to address the lack of major children's facilities in the region, which were previously only available at Bristol Children's Hospital and Musgrove Park Hospital in Taunton. The hospital benefits from the support of several voluntary organizations. The League of Friends, an active volunteer group, staffs the hospital shop and raises funds for various hospital projects. The Freewheelers Emergency Voluntary Service provides out-of-hours transport for blood, diagnostic specimens, and medications using motorcycles. Sunshine Radio, a hospital radio station run by volunteers, also serves the hospital. Additionally, Weston General Hospital collaborates closely with Weston Hospicecare, a nearby hospice that offers palliative care for patients with life-threatening conditions such as cancer. The new children's centre was partially funded by a community appeal called Weston Super Kids, which received widespread support, including from the town's Mayor, who made it her chosen charity during her term in office.
